sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **All-India Federation**: Proposed a union of British Indian Provinces and Princely States, though it never materialized due to the refusal of Princely States.
• **Provincial Autonomy**: Abolished **Dyarchy** in provinces and introduced 'Provincial Autonomy', granting provinces independent legal status.
• **Dyarchy at Centre**: Introduced the principle of Dyarchy at the Federal level, dividing subjects into 'Reserved' (Governor-General) and 'Transferred' (Ministers).
• **Key Metric**: The Act comprised 321 Sections and 10 Schedules, making it the lengthiest act passed by the British Parliament at that time.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Division of powers into Federal, Provincial, and Concurrent lists.
Residuary powers vested in the Governor-General.
Prelims: Source of the 7th Schedule of the Indian Constitution.
Provinces gained executive and legislative independence from the Centre.
Responsible government introduced; Ministers accountable to the legislature.
Mains: Shift from centralized control to decentralized governance.

items.definition: Established in 1937 in Delhi to adjudicate disputes between the Centre and Provinces; precursor to the Supreme Court of India.
Established under the Act to control currency and credit in the country, ensuring financial stability.
Extended the principle of separate electorates to depressed classes, women, and labor, further deepening communal divisions.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Bicameralism**: Introduced in 6 out of 11 provinces (Bengal, Bombay, Madras, Bihar, Assam, United Provinces).
• **Public Service Commissions**: Established Federal, Provincial, and Joint Public Service Commissions.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: The Federation never came into existence; the Governor-General retained 'overriding powers' (veto/discretionary).
• **Solutions**: The Act provided the structural skeleton that was later adopted, adapted, and refined by the Constituent Assembly.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'F-A-R-P-A' (Federation, Autonomy, RBI, PSC, Abolition of Dyarchy).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Federation (All-India), Autonomy (Provincial), RBI (Central Bank), PSC (Public Service Commissions), Abolition (of Dyarchy in provinces).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses 'Dyarchy at the Centre' (1935 Act) with 'Dyarchy in Provinces' (1919 Act). Always remember: 1919 = Provincial Dyarchy; 1935 = Federal Dyarchy.
Mains Value Addition: Use the phrase 'The 1935 Act was a machine with strong brakes and no engine' (Jawaharlal Nehru) to critique the lack of real sovereignty.

keyTakeaways: The Act provided the legal framework for the transition to a federal structure.
It abolished provincial dyarchy but introduced it at the federal level.
It established the Federal Court and the Reserve Bank of India, both of which remain pillars of modern Indian governance.
